title: QuantaAlpha: An Evolutionary Framework for LLM-Driven Alpha Mining

task.value: Automated LLM-driven alpha factor mining that improves factors via trajectory-level evolution (mutation and crossover) under noisy, non-stationary markets.
task.quote: we propose QuantaAlpha, an evolutionary alpha mining framework that treats each end-to-end mining run as a trajectory and improves factors via trajectory-level mutation and crossover.

architecture.value: Multi-agent pipeline: diversified planning initialization, idea agent for hypotheses, factor agent producing symbolic AST expressions compiled to code with consistency verifier and complexity/redundancy gates, evaluation agent, self-evolution via mutation/crossover, final factor pool fed to LightGBM.
architecture.quote: Overview of the QuantaAlpha framework, which consists of four core components: (A) Diversified Planning Initialization for candidate hypotheses, (B) Factor Realization that instantiates hypotheses into executable factors with constraint gating, (C) Self-Evolution with mutation and crossover over evaluated trajectories

data.value: Daily OHLCV+vwap data via Qlib for CSI 300 (300 large-cap A-shares); zero-shot transfer to CSI 500 and S&P 500; target is next-day return.
data.quote: Factor construction utilizes six basic features—open, high, low, close, volume, and vwap—to predict the next-day return

window.value: Train Jan 1 2016–Dec 31 2020, validation Jan 1–Dec 31 2021, test Jan 1 2022–Dec 26 2025 (same for all markets).
window.quote: We adopt a chronological split with training (Jan. 1, 2016 to Dec. 31, 2020), validation (Jan. 1, 2021 to Dec. 31, 2021), and testing (Jan. 1, 2022 to Dec. 26, 2025).

models.value: Backbone LLMs Qwen3-235B, DeepSeek-V3.2, Gemini-3-Pro-Preview, Claude-4.5-Sonnet, GPT-5.2 (DeepSeek-V3.2 default); LightGBM as downstream model.
models.quote: we evaluate multiple backbone LLMs, including Qwen3-235B, DeepSeek-V3.2, Gemini-3-Pro-Preview, Claude-4.5-Sonnet, and GPT-5.2. Unless otherwise specified, all other LLM-based experiments in this paper adopt DeepSeek-V3.2 for consistency and fair comparison.

baselines.value: ML models (Linear, MLP, LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, DoubleEnsemble), deep learning (GRU, LSTM, Transformer, TRA), factor libraries (Alpha158, Alpha360), LLM agents RD-Agent and AlphaAgent.
baselines.quote: We compare QuantaAlpha against four baseline categories: traditional machine learning models, deep learning time-series models, classical factor libraries, and LLM-based factor research agents, including RD-Agent and AlphaAgent.

headline_result.value: With GPT-5.2 on CSI 300 test period (2022–2025): IC 0.0472, ARR 4.68%, MDD 11.80%; transfer cumulative excess return about 40.28% (CSI 500) and 19.1% (S&P 500) over four years.
headline_result.quote: Using GPT-5.2, QuantaAlpha achieves the best IC at 0.0472, delivers an ARR of 4.68%, and maintains a low MDD of 11.80%.

costs.value: Buy 0.05%, sell 0.15% (0.20% round-trip), sensitivity at 1.5x and 2.0x; ~1.8M tokens and ~20 hours per main run via hosted APIs.
costs.quote: we adopt a standard transaction-cost setting with a buying cost of 0.05% (open_cost=0.0005) and a selling cost of 0.15% (close_cost=0.0015), corresponding to a 0.20% round-trip cost.

uncertainty.value: Three initial seed combinations (IC std 0.0021); daily IC t-tests over 966 trading days with 95% CIs, p<0.001.
uncertainty.quote: In particular, the standard deviations of IC and Rank IC are 0.0021 and 0.0024, respectively, suggesting that QuantaAlpha’s performance is not driven by a fortuitously selected seed set.

leakage_controls.value: Factor pool admission uses only 2021 validation RankIC; 2022–2025 test window never accessed during evolution or pool construction; chronological split.
leakage_controls.quote: The RankIC gate for pool admission is computed exclusively on the 2021 validation period; the 2022–2025 test window is never accessed during evolution or pool construction.

limitations.value: Real-world deployment would need additional transaction-cost modeling, risk control and live trading validation; performance decays after ~15 iterations.
limitations.quote: although real-world deployment would require additional transaction-cost modeling, risk control, and live trading validation.

release.value: Data and code released on GitHub.
release.quote: Data and code are available at https://github.com/QuantaAlpha/QuantaAlpha.
